title: the-deposit-rides-the-read
intention: DEPOSIT AS PHYSICS — the loop's last prose step retires. Today the exit gate shape-checks the verdict artifact on disk, but nothing forces its deposit into the trees (sail steps 6-7 are discipline; the what-killed-which counsel starves if a builder forgets). This stone makes the deposit a consequence of the crossing: the exit-gate-clean PROVED crossing appends the verdict berth path to an append-only pending ledger (file-only, instance-space — the fire path stays tree-free, so a netns-sealed crossing still enqueues identically), and the next entry through chart.live's one door drains pending deposits before serving (the read is the event — compile-on-read, never a clock, never a daemon). A verdict that never reached the tree stops being a lapse and becomes a measurable pending entry.
why: build_inspector charter edge (l) verbatim: 'the exit gate's verdict deposit is still discipline: the gate shape-checks the artifact on disk, but the live learn deposit of it is not forced (coupling emit to the db/embed hosts would break netns sealing); wants an event-shaped stone.' The netns constraint is why the deposit cannot ride the crossing directly — so the crossing writes the cheap durable half (a file) and the tree side pays the db cost at its own door, on its own next read. Same trust-transfer arc as both gates (the 64% stake): every discipline the chokepoint enforces is discipline no model spends context remembering.
traces_to: Law 4 — retires edge (l) / proved-answers-the-chart edge (a) from prose IOU into the chokepoint + the live door
Law 1 — drain fires on a read that already happens; the ledger is checked exactly when the tree is next consulted, never on a clock
Law 7 — the ledger is append-only and a failed deposit leaves its pending entry standing and loud; nothing pending is silently dropped
Law 6 — the ledger has exactly one writer; whose gate that is (emit's side or the chart device's) is the constrain question, answered before code

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate: teeth beside the code — an exit-gate-clean PROVED crossing appends exactly one ledger entry and the fire path gains no tree/db/embed import (nexus pin extended); a netns-sealed crossing still enqueues; the live door drains pending entries before serving and the deposit lands with provenance; a failed deposit leaves the pending entry standing; a second drain never double-deposits (idempotence by provenance, not by mutating the ledger). Tester netns seal. Live gate: this stone's own verdict deposit rides its own ledger.
falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: an exit-gate-clean PROVED crossing that leaves no pending entry; the crossing fire path importing tree/db/embed machinery; the drain mutating or truncating the ledger in place; a failed deposit vanishing instead of standing pending; a re-drain double-depositing the same berth; the drain firing on a clock or process that is not an existing read.
falsifier.horizon: re-read the MOMENT the embed ceiling is settled — one verdict stands pending on the real ledger right now and every chart door entry prints DEPOSIT FAILED until it lands; this ticket closes by draining it, not by re-proving the machinery. Then: when berth deposits (sail step 7's remaining discipline — the seven chart berths) want the same ledger; when verdict multiplicity (proved-answers-the-chart edge (b)) lands; when the pending ledger wants a diagnostic surface (how many verdicts are waiting, and how old).

chart_notes.constrain: ownership of the ledger (Law 6): emit appends it, chart.live drains it — one writer, whose gate, and where it berths in instance-space; also whether 'drained' is marked at all or derived (pending = ledger minus tree provenance), since a record of truth is never edited in place
chart_notes.survey: what the crossing record and the verdict artifact already carry that the ledger would duplicate — compose the existing journal/berth machinery, never a parallel record; and what deposit idempotence the live door already has
chart_notes.hypothesize: STANDING HYPOTHESIS 2026-07-31, unkilled and now the sharpest thing on this ticket: the 11283-char rendering refused against a ~7400-char practical ceiling is ONE defect surfacing in TWO places. The congruency corpus measured the same week averages 8766 chars per charter with cairn/machines/chart at 28212 — i.e. the median Cairn charter is already at the ceiling and the largest are 4x past it. If that is one defect, then bounding a rendering against an embed context is not a deposit-face problem at all; it is a chunking problem the whole system has and has been reading as a capacity error. Falsifier: if verdict artifacts embed cleanly once bounded but charters still refuse, they are two defects and this note is wrong.
